interest: Features a wartime German intelligence report on zaibatsu combines alongside SCAP regulations and foreign property restitution.
overview: This file documents U.S. State Department and SCAP monitoring, regulation, and reorganization of Japanese corporations and zaibatsu combines between 1945 and 1948. It contains a translated wartime German intelligence report detailing the organization and wartime role of major Japanese combines, alongside official SCAP reports and directives—notably SCAPIN 408 and 408/1—imposing asset freezes, operational restrictions, and criminal penalties on restricted concerns. Additionally, the records document private trade restrictions, travel permit procedures, and diplomatic efforts regarding foreign business interests and property restitution, highlighting cases involving Paramount Films, Toyo Menka Kaisha, and C. F. Sharp and Company.
